name_note: GTDB splits the classical genus Treponema into several genera, of which Treponema_D is one; the findings cited here concern gut-associated Treponema in the broad sense, including Treponema succinifaciens.

sentences.text: Treponema succinifaciens has been described as a strictly anaerobic, apathogenic member of the genus Treponema that oxidizes carbohydrates.
Its genome of 2,897,425 bp with one plasmid was reported as only the second completed and published type strain genome from the genus Treponema.
A 16S amplicon survey of rural and urban populations reported that the gut microbiota of all traditional rural populations studied was enriched with Treponema succinifaciens.
That study also reported that Spirochaetae were only present in the gut microbiota of individuals from traditional rural societies.
A shotgun metagenomic study of 1,801 women in Burkina Faso, Ghana, Kenya and South Africa reported Treponema species loss in urban populations, possibly driven by antibiotic susceptibility.
